To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neutrino masses are predicted to be of the order of 0.01 eV, the mixing angles are predicted to be in agreement with the present data, and a ν e − ν µ oscillation is suggested to be responsible for the solar neutrino puzzle.
a realistic pattern of fermions masses and mixings can be obtained in a supersymmetric Grand Unifying Theory invariant under the interchange between any SU(5) or SO(10).

a realistic fermion mass spectrum is obtained as a consequence of the existence of a large number of degenerate vacua, that the three neutrinos can be massless, that a solution to the solar neutrino puzzle is suggested and, finally, that a string theory framework could be a possible source of such a theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the physics of flavour and the possible connection between flavour and the structure of space-time.
the study of the phenomenological consequences of the following hypothesis: there is no preferred generation in nature, i.e. the three generations of quarks and leptons are completely equivalent.
the study of the physics beyond the Standard Model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory is not excluded by any of the present experimental data.
the theory is consistent with all the experimental data and that it predicts some interesting features which could be tested in forthcoming experiments.

, if the SO(10)-based model is realized in nature, then neutrino oscillations are predicted to occur and the ν e − ν τ mass splitting is predicted to be of the order of the solar neutrinos mass scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if the GUT symmetry breaking scale is not too far from the string scale, then the fermion mass and mixing pattern could be explained by a string GUT with a flavour symmetry.
the fermion masses and the mixing angles are determined by a few parameters and that the neutrino masses and mixings are determined by a single scale.
a string theory based on SO(10) or SU(5) could be consistent with the observed fermion masses and the solar neutrino puzzle, and could be testable by forthcoming experiments on the ν μ − ν e mixing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flavour structure of the Standard Model could be a consequence of a symmetry of the underlying theory, which is broken by a discrete degeneracy of its vacuum states.
the flavour symmetry of a theory can be used to predict fermion masses and mixing angles.

a flavour symmetric G U T, in spite of its apparent simplicity, can be a viable candidate for the unification of all the fermion masses and mixing angles, and for a solution of the neutrino mass problem.
